description.narrative: The Strengthening Gender Inclusive Initiatives Project aims to increase access to sustainable gender-responsive social services in Maldives by (i) improving gender equality and social inclusion (GESI) statistics; (ii) integrating gender-responsive budgeting (GRB) into government systems; (iii) strengthening the capacity of the social service system for aged care, early childcare, and domestic violence and gender-based violence (DV/GBV) services; (iv) establishing partnerships to support DV/GBV prevention, access to DV/GBV services, and aged care; and (v) constructing three climate-resilient shelters for DV/GBV survivors in Addu, Hulhumale, and Raa-Ungoofaaru. The project and attached TA will benefit women DV/GBV survivors and their dependent children and reduce the unpaid care burden on women caring for older family members and young children.

At least 20% of target government policy makers reported readiness for change, adopted new policies, and applied new competencies Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: PMU fully staffed as of August 2024 and operating well. Once the midterm report is submitted (2026), further analysis on this indicators progress can be more accurately gauged. Data Source: Impact Evaluation

At least 75% of DV/GBV survivors who requested shelter received services at stand-alone shelters Achievement: 20 Progress/Status: On track but implementation schedule changed. Construction for Output 5 to be staggered to allow for O&M budget for the Shelters to be allocated incrementally from 2026 onwards as a mitigation measure for projects sustainability in the face a of emerging countrywide fiscal risk. Works will commence in order of priority due to the risk of budget constraints: (i) Addu; (ii) Hulhumalé, and if financing allows; (iii) Raa. Addu Package contract was awarded in Q4 2025 with construction expected from Q2 2026 after finalization of construction documents. Data Source: Project monitoring and evaluation reports, MGFSS annual reports

Government-approved annual budget for DV/GBV, aged care, and childcare services increased by 10%. Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: MSFD's budget has been increasing annually since project approval, however, countrywide fiscal position is an emerging risk. During July 2025 review mission, the MOF Fiscal Affairs Department and MSFD State Minister confirmed the project grant and estimated Asset Management (AM) budget is included in the country budget exercise for 2024-2025 as an ongoing project as well as O&M costs from 2026 year onwards has been included in annual budget exercise. Data Source: Approved annual budget of the government.
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Capacity of the social service system strengthened for aged care, early childcare, and DV/GBV services Indicator: At least 10 MGFSS senior management (50% women) reported increased leadership skills Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: New TL commenced in Male on July 2025. Output: Capacity of the social service system strengthened for aged care, early childcare, and DV/GBV services Indicator: At least 75% of target management and staff (60% women) reported increase in knowledge and skills to deliver services at DV/GBV shelters, aged care and childcare Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: New TL commenced in Male on July 2025.. Output: Climate-resilient shelters for DV/GBV survivors established Indicator: By 2025, 3 climate-resilient, gender-responsive shelters for DV/GBV survivors (Addu, Hulhumalé, and Raa-Ungoofaaru) built and operational Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: Bidding Documents of Addu package was tendered in Dec 2025 taking into consideration i) concept design addendum following shelter rationalization exercise and ii) bid and performance security options revised. Draft Bid documents for Hulhumale are being finalized following the revised DDR. Raa is third priority for construction depending on grant financing envelope. PMU to monitor project cost estimates. Data Source: Project monitoring and evaluation reports, MGFSS and MNPHI construction progress reports and annual reports
